h1: The 4 Best LG Cordless Vacuums of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best LG Cordless Vacuums 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: four LG CordZero cordless vacuums compared on listed runtime, form factor and price tier, with a pick for every home.
summary: The LG CordZero with a 120 minute listed runtime is the best LG cordless vacuum, the longest figure of the four, in the $200 to $500 bucket. The second CordZero lists 100 minutes and a handheld mode, the older CordZero stick is the cheapest at $100 to $200, and the Q3 is the newest name with no published runtime.
intro: The commonest LG cordless mistake is buying on the name. LG sells several CordZero generations side by side, and the listings read almost alike while runtime and price tier differ. A shopper who sees CordZero and clicks the first result can end up with a model that runs twenty minutes less, or one that costs a tier more than it should for the same numbers.

Our editors ranked four LG sticks from their spec pages, scoring them on the Primea framework with listed runtime, form, generation and price tier weighted most. Prices are buckets. Suction power and filtration are not published for these listings, so we do not rank on them, and we flag the one model whose runtime is missing.

products.name: LG CordZero Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The longest listed runtime of any LG here makes it the easy default.
products.description:
This CordZero stick lists a 120 minute runtime, the longest figure among the four LG models we ranked. It sits in the $200 to $500 bucket and is sold as a cordless stick. Runtime matters because a big home can need two full passes, and a vacuum that dies halfway leaves a stripe of carpet undone.

It ranks above the other stick because of that runtime and its current line status, while the handheld-capable model trails by 20 minutes at the same tier. The older stick costs less but offers 100 minutes.

Buy it for larger homes that want fewer charging stops. The caveats are that it costs more than the older stick and the runtime shrinks at max power. Skip it if your space is small and a cheaper stick covers it.
products.idealFor: Owners of larger homes who want fewer charging stops.
products.skipIf: Your space is small and a cheaper stick covers it.

products.name: LG CordZero Vacuum
products.verdict: A 100 minute CordZero that also lists a handheld mode.
products.description:
This CordZero lists 100 minutes of runtime and a handheld configuration, in the $200 to $500 bucket. A handheld mode lets the motor and bin detach from the pole, which makes stairs, car seats and sofas far easier than wrestling a full-length stick.

It ranks second because it trails the top pick by 20 minutes of listed runtime while costing the same tier. What it adds is the handheld listing, which neither of the other sticks states.

Buy it for one tool that handles floors and small jobs. The caveats are the same tier with less runtime than the leader and bundle contents that vary. Skip it if you want the longest possible runtime.
products.idealFor: Buyers who want one tool for floors and small jobs.
products.skipIf: You want the longest possible runtime.

products.name: LG CordZero Cordless Stick Vacuum
products.verdict: The cheapest LG here, with the same 100 minute runtime as the pricier handheld.
products.description:
This older CordZero stick lists 100 minutes of runtime and lands in the $100 to $200 bucket, a full tier below the top two. It is a plain cordless stick with the same listed runtime as the handheld-capable model.

It ranks third because it gives up the 120 minute figure of the leader, but it also saves real money. An older generation usually means fewer refinements, though the listing names none that matter. Against the handheld model, it matches the minutes for less.

Buy it for apartments where LG on a tighter budget makes sense. The caveats are an older generation and no handheld listing. Skip it if you want the newest generation.
pros: Lowest price tier of the LGs
products.idealFor: Apartment owners who want LG on a tighter budget.

products.name: LG Cordzero Q3 Cordless Stick Vacuum Cleaner with Auto Multi-Surface
products.verdict: The Q3 is the newest name, but its listing gives us the least to compare.
products.description:
The Q3 is a cordless stick with an auto multi-surface label, priced in the $200 to $500 bucket. Auto multi-surface suggests the vacuum adjusts to floor type, though the listing does not explain how, and a feature name is not a performance claim.

It ranks last only because its listing publishes no runtime figure. The three models above give a number, and a vacuum you cannot size against your home is a gamble. It may well be the best of the four, but the page does not show it.

Buy it for homes that mix hard floors and rugs, after you confirm the runtime. The caveats are the missing runtime and the same tier as the leaders. Skip it if you need a published figure before buying.
products.idealFor: Homes that mix hard floor and rugs.
products.skipIf: You need a published runtime before buying.

methodology.title: Listed runtime
methodology.description: We compared the minutes each LG listing publishes, since runtime decides how much floor one charge covers.

methodology.title: Form factor
methodology.description: We checked whether the listing sells a stick, a handheld mode or both, because that sets how many jobs the vacuum can do.

whatMatters.detail: Runtime is how many minutes the vacuum runs on a full battery. It matters because a short runtime means mid-clean charging stops in bigger homes. Find the minutes in the listing bullets and treat them as the best case, since the strongest power mode usually drains the battery faster than the figure suggests. Plan on a charging stop in a large home.

Some cordless vacuums detach from the pole and become a hand tool. That matters for stairs, upholstery and cars, where a full stick is awkward. Look for a handheld mention in the listing title or specs, and note that only one of the four LG listings states it. Without it, expect a full-length stick for everything.

LG keeps older and newer CordZero models on sale together, with similar names. A newer generation can change features, while an older one usually costs less. Compare the model name and the price tier rather than trusting the brand line, and check dates or series letters when the listing gives them. A newer name is not always a better vacuum.

Homes with both hard floor and rugs benefit from a vacuum that adapts to surfaces. An auto multi-surface label suggests this, but it is a feature name, not a promise. Read the listing description to see what it actually does, and be cautious about paying extra for the label.

A listing with clear numbers lets you compare models on paper. When a figure like runtime is missing, you are guessing. Prefer models that state their specs, or confirm the missing number before buying, and ask the seller if the page is silent, since a published figure is the minimum, and a refusal to give one is itself a warning.

faq.q: Are all four of these actual LG vacuums?
faq.a: Yes. Each carries the LG CordZero or Cordzero name in its listing, and we dropped other brands from the comparison. Look-alike listings from sellers using the name loosely were left out entirely.

faq.q: Is the 120 minute model worth it over the 100 minute one?
faq.a: Only if your home needs the extra time. The 100 minute stick is in a cheaper bucket and covers an apartment, while the 120 minute model suits a larger house. Neither number is a promise, so match it to the size of your floors.

faq.q: Why does the Q3 rank last?
faq.a: Its listing gives no runtime figure, so it cannot be compared on paper. It may still suit mixed floors, but verify the minutes first. A vacuum with no stated runtime is hard to size against a real home.
It lets the vacuum come off the pole for stairs, cars and furniture. The LG CordZero Vacuum is the one that lists it, so it suits homes with many stairs.

faq.q: How should I read the runtime numbers?
faq.a: Treat them as the best case. Stronger suction settings usually shorten the real minutes, so plan for less than 120 or 100. Use the lowest power setting for long sessions to stretch the battery.

faq.q: Do the two CordZero sticks differ?
faq.a: They share a name but differ in listed runtime (120 versus 100 minutes) and price tier. Check the model before ordering, because paying the higher tier for the 100 minute stick is the mistake to avoid.

finalTake: Buy the 120 minute CordZero for a larger home, and the 100 minute handheld model if you want one tool for floors and upholstery. The older stick is the budget route for an apartment. The Q3 is the one to verify before buying, because its listing gives no runtime. Treat every runtime as a best case.
